title: Most people skip over this story.
paragraphs: Most people skip over this story.

It’s tucked into a complicated chapter in Genesis.
A strange moment during childbirth.
A tiny detail about a scarlet thread.
But hidden in this moment is a lesson that speaks to anyone who has ever felt behind, overlooked, or second in line.
The story happens in Genesis 38:27–30.
When the time came for Tamar to give birth, everyone in the room expected a normal delivery.
But what happened next surprised everyone.
During labor, one of the twins pushed out his hand first.
The midwife immediately reacted.
In the ancient world, the firstborn mattered deeply. The firstborn carried inheritance rights, family leadership, and generational blessing.
So the midwife tied a scarlet thread around the baby’s wrist to mark him as the firstborn.
The message was clear:
“This one came first.”
But then something unexpected happened.
The hand pulled back.
And suddenly another child pushed forward and was born first.
The midwife responded in amazement:
“What a breakthrough you have made!”
So they named him Perez.
His name literally means “breakthrough” or “to burst forth.”
Think about that moment.

The one who looked like he would be second…
became the firstborn.

The one who appeared to come after…
became the one who broke through.
This is not just an unusual birth story.
It reveals something powerful about how God works.
Throughout Scripture, God repeatedly overturns human expectations.
The world assumes that position determines destiny.
But God often chooses differently.
Abel’s offering was accepted over Cain’s.
Isaac carried the promise instead of Ishmael.
Jacob received the blessing instead of Esau.
Joseph rose above his older brothers.
David was chosen while his stronger brothers were overlooked.
And here in Tamar’s story, the child who seemed second became the one who came first.
God does not always follow human order.
And that truth speaks directly to many people today.
Some people feel like they started life with disadvantages.
Others feel like someone else always gets the opportunity first.
Some people feel overlooked, forgotten, or behind.
But the story of Perez reminds us of something important:
Your starting position does not determine your final purpose.
You might feel like life tied the scarlet thread to someone else.
Someone else got the promotion.
Someone else got the opportunity.
Someone else seems ahead of you.
But God is not limited by the order people expect.
In one unexpected moment, everything changed.
The hand that appeared first did not determine the outcome.
The breakthrough did.
And here is another powerful detail many people miss.
Perez didn’t just become the firstborn that day.
His story continued far beyond that tent.
When the genealogy of the Messiah is recorded in the Gospel of Matthew, Perez appears in the lineage leading to Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:3).
The child who looked like he would come second became part of the line that would bring the Savior into the world.
That means the breakthrough at birth was only the beginning of a much larger purpose.
Sometimes God allows us to feel behind for a season.
Sometimes life looks like someone else got ahead.
Sometimes the story appears already decided.
But God has a way of rewriting moments that look settled.
The scarlet thread marked the hand that appeared first.
But heaven marked the one who would break through.
And that leads to a question worth thinking about today.
Are there areas in your life where you feel like you came second?
A dream.
A calling.
An opportunity.
A season where you feel like someone else moved ahead of you.
The story of Tamar’s twins reminds us of this truth:
God is not limited by the order people expect.
Sometimes the one who seemed second is the one God has prepared for breakthrough.
Sometimes the story isn’t finished when people think it is.
And sometimes the moment that looks like you’re behind…
…is actually the moment before the breakthrough.
The hand appeared first.
But the breakthrough came next.
And when God writes the story, the ending can surprise everyone.
Have you ever experienced a moment where God changed the outcome you thought was already decided?
